summary: REFUTE stage fan-out: the Level selects the required independent adversaries. DRY runs at every Level; L1 runs all five, L2 runs Prove-It, DRY, and Lie-catcher with optional Laziness-auditor, and L3 runs DRY with an optional human-requested Lie-catcher. Produces one verdict per required lens; any FAIL blocks the gate.

Searched for a second, competing implementation of each of the 8 files the artifact claims RULE-PHASE already shipped (EngineAssembly, BoundaryAdapterFactories, OneDoorRule, DeclaredTypeScanner, SymbolResolution, WrittenNameScanner, EngineToBoundariesOneDoorAnalyzer, EngineInternalsOneDoorAnalyzer) — each exists exactly once with exactly one class definition.

Searched src/ outside SystemServices.cs for a second direct `TimeProvider.System` read that would mean the AG0015-guarded primitive was duplicated rather than reused behind its one approved owner — found none.

Diffed all six of the artifact's verbatim contract quotations (cited at lines 229, 231, 16, 244, 110, 234) against the live contract.md text at those exact lines to catch a drifted second copy of contract wording — all six are byte-for-byte matches.

Searched the whole repository for architecture-lie-catcher-review.json, which the artifact twice claims exists as its fresh Lie-catcher review — not found anywhere; the only similarly-named file belongs to an unrelated, already-completed 2026-09-01 run-record. This is an evidence-completeness gap outside the DRY lens's duplication scope, so it does not change this verdict, but it is flagged here for the Lie-catcher lens.

findings.summary: architecture-result.md:23 presents an enumeration of the contract's new Surfaces files as exhaustive when it is not, and its attached shipped-everything claim is false of the real set — the same defect class (a partial inspection described as complete) that failed the second authoring run.
findings.evidence: architecture-result.md:23 reads, verbatim: "Every genuinely new file in the contract's Surfaces — `EngineAssembly.cs`, `BoundaryAdapterFactories.cs`, `OneDoorRule.cs`, `DeclaredTypeScanner.cs`, `SymbolResolution.cs`, `WrittenNameScanner.cs`, `EngineToBoundariesOneDoorAnalyzer.cs`, `EngineInternalsOneDoorAnalyzer.cs` — is analyzer surface assigned to RULE-PHASE by contract step 3, and RULE-PHASE has shipped all of them." The contract's Surfaces names six further genuinely new files that the eight omit. contract.md:188 (`sed -n '188p'`): "...and two new files, `analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/EngineToBoundariesOneDoorAnalyzerTests.cs` and `analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/EngineInternalsOneDoorAnalyzerTests.cs`." — the contract itself calls them new files; neither is in the enumeration. contract.md:185 (`sed -n '185p'`): "- `analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/SymbolResolutionTests.cs`, `analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/WrittenNameScannerTests.cs`, `analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/DeclaredTypeScannerTests.cs`, and `analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/TypeTreeTests.cs` — direct tests..." — four more, none enumerated. The "RULE-PHASE has shipped all of them" half is false of the complete set: `[ -f ]` on each returns MISSING for analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/SymbolResolutionTests.cs, analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/DeclaredTypeScannerTests.cs, and analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/TypeTreeTests.cs (only WrittenNameScannerTests.cs, EngineToBoundariesOneDoorAnalyzerTests.cs and EngineInternalsOneDoorAnalyzerTests.cs exist). The artifact contradicts itself on this at its own line 76: "`remaining-work.md` carries the three tests assigned to TDD: the direct helper tests for shared resolution and declaration scanning, the pointer-traversal test for `TypeTree.Any`...", and remaining-work.md:7,9,13 names exactly those three unshipped Surfaces files. The eight files listed do check out individually — all eight exist on disk, and contract.md:228 (step 3) does assign them (`SymbolResolution`/`WrittenNameScanner` responsibilities, "Add `EngineAssembly.cs`, `BoundaryAdapterFactories.cs`, and `OneDoorRule.cs`", "add AG0040 and AG0041" = EngineToBoundariesOneDoorAnalyzer.cs:30 `DiagnosticId = "AG0040"` and EngineInternalsOneDoorAnalyzer.cs:39 `DiagnosticId = "AG0041"`, "Extract `DeclaredTypeScanner`") — it is the universal quantifier and the shipped-all claim that are untrue.

findings.summary: The build evidence at architecture-result.md:31-48 is a hand-written reconstruction presented inside `$`-prompt terminal-transcript blocks; one diagnostic line appears in no captured output, and the run folder holds no build log for either build.
findings.evidence: architecture-result.md:47 renders the no-override diagnostic as "error AG0015 ... src/AgentGuard.Boundaries/SystemServices.cs(88,30)". My own re-run in an isolated copy produces the line in the opposite order and no other form: "<REPO>/src/AgentGuard.Boundaries/SystemServices.cs(88,30): error AG0015: Clock access 'TimeProvider.System' bypasses the injected clock; read time off ISystemServices.Clock — a raw wall-clock read is banned everywhere and a direct TimeProvider acquisition only at the composition point [<REPO>/src/AgentGuard.Boundaries/AgentGuard.Boundaries.csproj]". The stage's actual capture (session scratchpad arch-build.txt, lines 34-36) carries the same real wording and carries no EXIT line at all, so the "EXIT=0"/"EXIT=1" lines shown in the transcript blocks appear in no captured output either. `.dev/inprocess/74-pre-work-move-system-services/` contains no build log for either build. architecture.js:1389 defines the stage's build proof as "buildProof (pasted with exit code)". The recorded numbers are nevertheless all true — my re-run of `dotnet build -c Release -p:WarningsNotAsErrors=AG0015` gave EXIT=0, "1 Warning(s) / 0 Error(s)", the single diagnostic AG0015 at SystemServices.cs(88,30) and no other warning or error identifier in the whole log; my re-run of `dotnet build -c Release` on a cleaned tree gave EXIT=1, "0 Warning(s) / 1 Error(s)", error AG0015 at the same location. The defect is the presentation of reconstructed text as captured output, not the arithmetic.

refutationAttempts: Tried to refute the Program.Main correction as a reword rather than a fix: read the live declaration. src/AgentGuard.Cli/Program.cs:59 is `    private static Task<int> Main(string[] args)` and Program.cs:23 is `internal sealed class Program`. Both match the artifact's line 54 exactly, including the cited line numbers. Genuinely corrected, not reworded.

Tried to find a second or generated Program declaration that could make `internal` defensible after all: `grep -rn --include='*.cs' "class Program" src tests analyzers eng` finds the CLI's sole declaration plus `ProgramCliTests` and six `internal static class Program` strings inside analyzer-test fixture sources (synthetic compilations, not the CLI assembly); `grep -n partial src/AgentGuard.Cli/Program.cs` finds nothing; no generated Program exists under src/AgentGuard.Cli/obj. The artifact's blanket phrase "There is one `Program` class in the tree" is loose against those fixture strings, but its operative qualifier — "with no partial or generated second declaration" — holds, and nothing material turns on it. Not raised as a finding.

Tried to refute the removal of the member inventory as cosmetic: grepped the artifact for any member list. None remains; architecture-result.md:58 states "This artifact states no member inventory for any class." Then counted the members it used to claim: Program.cs declares exactly 15 (lines 25, 35, 44, 59, 65, 83, 96, 123, 138, 145, 152, 170, 207, 230, 253), and the three the history names as omitted (_args, the internal constructor, TryParseEvent) are among them — 15 total, 12 listed. The history's arithmetic checks out and the completeness claim is gone from the result. Genuinely corrected.

Tried to catch a doctored contract quotation: byte-compared all six quoted fragments against the live contract with a Python substring test. Lines 16, 110, 229, 231, 234 and 244 each contain the quoted text verbatim at the cited line; the only omissions are a leading list dash or step number, and line 244's is explicitly elided with an ellipsis. No quote is altered, invented, or mis-cited.

Tried to refute the build evidence by re-running both builds myself rather than trusting the record. rsync'd the tree (minus bin/obj/.git) to the scratchpad and verified src/, tests/ and analyzers/ are byte-identical to the shared checkout (`diff -rq` clean, 249/105/151 .cs files each side). `dotnet build -c Release -p:WarningsNotAsErrors=AG0015` → EXIT=0, "1 Warning(s) / 0 Error(s)", all 14 solution projects produced DLLs, and `grep -oE "(warning|error) [A-Za-z]+[0-9]+" | sort -u` over the entire log returns exactly one token: "warning AG0015". Cleaned every bin/obj and ran `dotnet build -c Release` → EXIT=1, "0 Warning(s) / 1 Error(s)", the same AG0015 at SystemServices.cs(88,30). Every recorded number reproduces, and because the override only demotes AG0015 while everything else still fails the build, the clean override build proves it masks nothing else.

Tried to find a suppression used to reach green: `git diff -U0 -- analyzers src tests eng | grep -E '^\+.*(pragma warning|SuppressMessage|NoWarn|severity *= *none|WarningsNotAsErrors|TreatWarningsAsErrors)'` returns nothing; grepping the ten new/renamed analyzer files finds one hit only, a documentation comment at WrittenNameScanner.cs:73; `grep -rn AG0015` across *.props, *.targets, *.editorconfig and *.csproj returns nothing. The AG0015 handling is the sanctioned `-p:WarningsNotAsErrors` mechanism rails-run-a-workflow names, with the diagnostic left enabled and visible.

Tried to refute the claim that this stage touched no code: `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- src tests` is empty, and mtimes show the newest non-obj source write anywhere in src/tests/analyzers at 2026-09-15 20:00, before contract.md (20:28) and both artifacts (20:54). Nothing under src/ or tests/ was created or modified and no analyzer was edited during the correction.

Tried to refute the no-signature determination as work avoided: contract.md:229 authorizes "record the contract-backed no-signature result if applicable"; the approved decision block at contract.md:111 says "If no further signature changes are needed, report and review that result rather than inventing additional interfaces"; contract.md:244 forbids adding service interfaces or container members; contract.md:231 assigns the SystemServices move to IMPLEMENT; and the whole Surfaces section (contract.md:172-192) contains no new application interface, DTO or enum — only a file move, csproj edits, `using` changes and analyzer/test work. rails-run-a-workflow:154 defines exactly this result shape (empty skeletonFiles and perType, the no-signature explanation, contract evidence, then the same panel). The determination is the contract-required outcome.

Tried to catch the history file relabelling a failure: architecture-history.md:3 states "Neither run below is an accepted result. Both failed their independent panel", and each run keeps its verdicts (run 1: "Lie-catcher FAIL on two findings, DRY FAIL on one, SOLID PASS"; run 2: "SOLID PASS, DRY PASS, Lie-catcher FAIL on two findings"). No relabelling. Its two run ids appear nowhere else in the repo, so the panel records themselves are not on disk, but nothing in it is stated as passing that failed.

Tried to catch a weakened, deleted or skipped test hiding behind the two deleted test files in `git status`: the deletions are the contract-mandated renames at contract.md:188. BoundariesToCrossPlatformOneDoorAnalyzerTests.cs went from 3 [Fact]s at HEAD to 19 in OneDoorIntoCrossPlatformAnalyzerTests.cs; BoundariesToPerOsOneDoorAnalyzerTests.cs from 4 to 20 in OneDoorIntoPerOsAnalyzerTests.cs; GuardedConstructionAnalyzerTests.cs 19→20; TimeMustUseTimeProviderAnalyzerTests.cs 10→12. `grep -rn 'Skip *=|\[Fact(Skip'` over the analyzer and application test trees returns nothing. No test was weakened, and none of it belongs to the artifact under review anyway.

Checked the decision-level items the artifact relies on for Tim's approval of that exact recorded wording: the AG0015 override sits at contract.md:110 under the recorded heading "Tim accepted RULE-PHASE and approved the ARCHITECTURE and TDD warning override, presented as written:", and the history explains it was moved into the contract after run 1 refused to build on an unrecorded approval — the correct direction of fix, not an invented approval. The corrected artifact adds no new decision-level item of its own.

Checked whether this stage owed an autoResolved array: rails-decisions scopes applied-principle evidence to GROUND explorer results, DESIGN proposals, the DESIGN verdict and the hidden-decision filter, and `grep -rn autoResolved .agents` shows the schema enforced only in design.js and refute-readiness.js — never in architecture.js. ARCHITECTURE owes none, and rails-run-a-workflow:209 confirms L3 supplies no stage output paths, which is why the recorded-results map handed to me was correctly empty.
